title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: for a morphism X→Y with geometric base points, Grothendieck writes E^T_X (his notation here for the fundamental group with base-point datum T) as an extension of E^T_Y by E^T_{X/Y}. E^T_{X/Y} plays the role of a 'geometric' π, and E^T_Y plays the role of an arithmetic profinite Galois group. The case of main interest is Y = Spec K, K a field.

This page, first paragraph: for Y = Spec K with geometric point ȳ = Spec K̄, the group E_Y = E^ȳ_Y 'is indeed' the absolute Galois group Gal(K̄/K), with K̄ the algebraic closure singled out by ȳ. He announces the short notation Γ, instead of Γ_K or Γ_K^{K̄} and instead of E_y. He remarks that this is especially apt when K is algebraic over the prime field. Then there are no 'geometric points' to distinguish from 'arithmetic points': the whole group is purely arithmetic.

Second paragraph: let K be a field (possibly algebraically closed), L a finitely generated extension of K, and X a proper regular model of L over K. Then π_1(X, L̄) = E_X^{L̄} is a quotient of Gal(L̄/L) = E_L^{L̄}, and this quotient does not depend on the chosen model X, 'as is well known'.

Modern justification: Spec L → X is dominant and X is normal, so π_1(Spec L) → π_1(X) is surjective. Its kernel corresponds to the étale L-algebras that extend to finite étale X-schemes. Given two proper regular models X, X', the birational map X ⇢ X' is defined off a closed subset of codimension ≥ 2, because X is normal and X' is proper. By Zariski–Nagata purity, a cover of X' pulled back to that open set extends to X. By symmetry the two kernels coincide.

The following page continues: this quotient is the 'universally given' (unramified) part of Gal(L̄/L). For an open model U = X∖Z there are surjections Gal(L̄/L) → π_1(U) → π_1(X). He then introduces decomposition and inertia groups at the generic points of the boundary divisors. The purpose is to set up the arithmetic-versus-geometric decomposition of fundamental groups of function fields, as groundwork for the anabelian / Galois–Teichmüller programme of the 'Longue Marche'.
errors: Strictly, Gal(K̄/K) should be read as Aut(K̄/K) ≅ Gal(K^sep/K); harmless.

The existence of a proper regular model of L/K is presupposed. In positive characteristic and dimension > 3 this depends on resolution of singularities, which is still open. The statement is safe only as 'for any such model, if one exists'.

The model-independence argument needs purity (Zariski–Nagata / SGA 2) together with the codimension-2 indeterminacy of rational maps from a normal scheme to a proper one. Grothendieck invokes it only as 'bien connu'; this is correct but not argued.

ideas.what: π_1 of Spec K with geometric point Spec K̄ equals the absolute Galois group; notation Γ; for K algebraic over the prime field the group is 'purely arithmetic'.
ideas.modern_name: Absolute Galois group as étale fundamental group of a point

ideas.what: π_1 of a proper regular model of a function field L/K is a quotient of Gal(L̄/L) independent of the model.
ideas.modern_name: Birational invariance of π_1 for proper regular schemes (via Zariski–Nagata purity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 1 X 3.4; SGA 2 X 3.4), building on Zariski–Nagata
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. X §3; SGA 2 Exp. X

deep.surprise_reason: Standard setup: the Galois group as π_1 of a point, and model-independence of the unramified quotient of Gal(L̄/L). Both are classical and in SGA 1/2. The page only fixes notation for the arithmetic/geometric extension studied in the Longue Marche notes.
transcription_corrections: 's'identifie tout [?] et bien [?] au groupe' should read 's'identifie bel et bien au groupe'.
'de [illegible] K̄/K': the word before K̄/K is heavily crossed out (probably 'l'extension').
'Sinon [?], on notera' is more likely 'Souvent, on notera'.
'au lieu de E_y — [illegible]': the illegible word is plausibly 'surtout'.
'Soit K [-est-] corps': a tilde-like mark is written above K, and the crossed-out word appears to be 'est', replaced by 'un'.
'L une ext. [?] de type fini de K': 'ext.' (extension) is the plausible reading.
